statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-54183 (GHSA-g4qj-5vxv-wggf): before Apache Airflow 3.3.1, the secrets masker's depth limit stopped it from descending into lists, tuples and sets nested beyond that limit, so an Airflow Variable holding a sensitive key inside such a deeply nested value was shown unmasked in the Variables UI. Upstream notes that any authenticated user who can see the Variable in the UI can already read its full value through the Variables REST API, so the masking is a defense against shoulder-surfing in the UI, not an access control. It is an incomplete-fix follow-up to CVE-2026-42358: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g4qj-5vxv-wggf, https://lists.apache.org/thread/z5mrdq6c60f2wyx4cc64cj8nv0dxd9lo. The fix is https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/68422, released in 3.3.1 as https://github.com/apache/airflow/commit/76961a04633f8e5b72e0042b797266ba650fc47c on the v3-3-test branch, which moves the list, tuple and set walk in _redact (shared/secrets_masker secrets_masker.py) ahead of the depth cutoff. The DHI Debian repository has 104 airflow packages, 3.3.0-0 to the current 3.4.0-11, for amd64 and arm64, and none in the DHI security repository. We downloaded and unpacked all 104, each checked against the repository index checksum. Each holds two copies of secrets_masker.py, under airflow/_shared/secrets_masker and airflow/sdk/_shared/secrets_masker, plus a compatibility module, airflow/sdk/execution_time/secrets_masker.py, that has no _redact. In the 3.3.0 builds (3.3.0-0 to 3.3.0-3, apache-airflow 3.3.0) both copies have the old code, with the depth cutoff ahead of the list and set walk. From 3.3.1-0 on, in every 3.3.1, 3.3.2 and 3.4.0 build (apache-airflow 3.3.1, 3.3.2 and 3.4.0), both copies have the fixed order. The 3.4.0 release carries the main-branch fix commit, https://github.com/apache/airflow/commit/4d39a855b1c6c3072e53b49465dc66f5a38e095a. FIXED is set at 3.3.1-0, the first build with the fix; the 3.3.0 builds are affected.
